name: Odds Ticker
description: Displays scrolling odds and betting lines for upcoming games across multiple sports leagues including NFL, NBA, MLB, NCAA Football, and more
author: ChuckBuilds

versions.notes: Saving settings in the web UI now takes effect the way a restart would. on_config_change re-applied speed through legacy setters that cleared the shared resolver's whole-pixel step while keeping the old frame hold, ignored league, favourite-team and filter changes, and skipped BasePlugin.on_config_change, so enabled went stale; it now re-runs the resolver, reloads leagues and filters, and refetches. get_display_duration() no longer fetches games, odds and rankings and rebuilds the strip on the render loop, Vegas and web-UI polling when no strip exists (every call off-season); it reports the cached duration and update() fetches. Odds requests use core's identifying session, a 5s timeout and a 60s cooldown after a failure, as core BaseOddsManager does. A .bdf face picked in customization now loads at its native size instead of silently falling back to PressStart2P. show_odds_only and multi-league soccer no longer stop collecting at max_games_per_league in two remaining places. ESPN 404/429/503 responses now reach their own handling (an error Response is falsy). A failed import of an unrelated optional core module no longer replaces ScrollHelper with a stub. display_manager.width replaces display_manager.matrix.width, which raised when the matrix failed to initialise. The plugin's log lines keep its plugin id. The fallback message fits a 64px panel. display_options.scroll_pixels_per_second (outranked by scroll_speed/scroll_delay, which always carry schema defaults) and display_options.target_fps (read by nothing) are deprecated and ignored: they stay in the schema as hidden properties, so configs that still carry them load and save valid. Removed the hand-rolled speed precedence and conversions the resolver superseded, the public set_scroll_speed/set_scroll_delay, and the unused _fetch_team_record.

Requires LEDMatrix core 3.4.0 or newer, because the ticker uses the new scroll frame pacing. Since #462 (2026-09-07) display() passes frame_hold to display_manager.set_scrolling_state(), an argument core 3.3.x does not have. The call sits inside the try that wraps the whole frame, so on those cores every frame raised TypeError, logged an error and drew the fallback message instead of the odds. The manifest still admitted any core from 2.0.0, so the store kept offering it there. The floor is now 3.4.0 (versions[0] and compatible_versions), so the store refuses the install on an older core and asks the user to update LEDMatrix first. A copy already installed on a 3.3.x core stays broken until that core is updated. No code change.

Adds filtering.favorite_weight (1-5, default 1). Favorite teams used to matter only with show_favorite_teams_only on; otherwise the ticker took each league's soonest max_games_per_league games, so a favorite's game could miss the ticker entirely and games_per_favorite_team did nothing. Above 1, each favorite's next games (up to games_per_favorite_team) always make their league's cut, with the soonest other games filling the rest, and each favorite game appears that many times in the scroll, its extra turns spread evenly around the loop. games_data stays one entry per game -- the weighting is applied only when the strip is composed, each game rendered once -- so live detection, update logging and odds fetches are unchanged. The candidate selection used for odds requests follows the same rule, so every guaranteed favorite is priced. The default keeps the old behaviour exactly.

Snap the large error-message font onto PressStart2P's 8px pixel grid (it was 10). Pixel faces rasterise cleanly only at whole multiples of their grid; off the grid the 1-bit rasteriser drops a column from every glyph. The ticker's own team/odds/datetime text was already on-grid at 8 and is unchanged.

Removes three modules nothing imported: odds_renderer.py (885 lines), data_fetcher.py (380) and game_filter.py (290). Rendering and fetching both live in manager.py; these were never wired up. Plugin modules are loaded as bare top-level names scoped to their own plugin, so nothing outside odds-ticker could reach them either. No behaviour change.

Per-game render tracing moved from INFO to DEBUG. _create_game_display() carried 12 INFO calls against 2 DEBUG -- width arithmetic and a four-line narration of every broadcast-logo paste -- and it runs once per game per rebuild. Measured on a 256x64 rig: 1,350 journal lines an hour from two of those calls alone, about 22% of everything the display service logged. One more per-game trace in _fetch_league_games() went with them. No behaviour change; run with DEBUG to get them back.

Stop the web UI's own team picker reporting the ticker as degraded. The four leagues that render as checkbox groups -- NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL -- are saved with a hidden companion field, so picking teams in the UI writes favorite_teams_data beside favorite_teams. The plugin never reads it, but every league object here set additionalProperties: false, so the core's schema check flagged all four and the web UI showed "Degraded: Config schema: Field 'leagues.nfl': Additional properties are not allowed ('favorite_teams_data' was unexpected)" and three more like it, on a config the UI itself had just written. The key is now permitted on every league -- unconstrained, since the widget has submitted it both as an array and as a JSON string -- while unknown keys are still rejected, so a typo in a hand-edited config is still caught. Affects only the schema; nothing about what the ticker fetches or draws changes.
versions.changelog: Permit the favorite_teams_data key the web UI writes beside favorite_teams, so picking teams no longer marks the plugin degraded

versions.notes: Portability fix and documentation. Two strftime calls used %-m, a glibc extension that raises ValueError on Windows and musl; the exception escaped _create_game_display and the whole ticker fell back to 'No odds data'. They now build the same text portably (#414 tracks the same pattern in ten other plugins). Bitmap fonts now load at their declared PIXEL_SIZE instead of silently swapping in another face, and cozette.bdf is dropped from the three font menus because the core ships no such file (#387). The README documented 8 settings at top level when the schema nests every one of them under display_options, data_settings or filtering -- and because additionalProperties is false, a config using those paths is rejected rather than ignored. Two of the eight also gave the wrong default. All 47 settings are now documented at their real paths, with real rendered screenshots.
versions.changelog: Publish the scroll cache array before the image, so a rebuild on the worker thread cannot be read half-applied

The college football rank badge now reads the top division's poll. ESPN answers the rankings endpoint with four blocks -- AP Top 25, the AFCA Coaches Poll, the FCS Coaches Poll and the AFCA Division II Poll -- and the ticker took whichever came first. That is AP today, so the table was FBS by luck rather than by choice: nothing in the payload promises the order and ESPN changes it, adding the CFP rankings in November. With a lower-division poll leading, the ticker would have drawn an FCS poll position beside an FBS team. ESPN's own order is kept among top-division polls; only the divisions below FBS are skipped. Ported from the same guard in football-scoreboard 3.0.0, which shares this rankings code.

Keep the ESPN refresh off the render thread. display() called _perform_update() inline, and that reaches _fetch_league_games and _fetch_team_rankings, both blocking HTTP calls -- so the marquee stalled for the length of the round trip. update() already guards this by checking is_currently_scrolling() and handing the work to defer_update(); display() now uses the same guard, so the refresh stops landing on the one thread it must not block.

Rebuild the ticker when something else clears its scroll cache. Vegas invalidates a plugin's cached scroll image whenever the plugin reports an update -- that is what stops last night's live game being redrawn -- but it cannot clear this plugin's own ticker_image, which is what display() tested to decide whether a rebuild was needed. Between the invalidation (about once a minute on a live rig) and this plugin's own next rebuild (an hour, whenever no game is live) the helper returned nothing and the panel showed "No odds data" over games it was holding perfectly well: ten such frames in three days of logs, with the games list never once actually empty.

Request odds only for the games the ticker can actually show. Odds were fetched inline for every game in the future_fetch_days window, and the list was trimmed to max_games_per_league afterwards -- five by default. Measured on a live rig during a college-football weekend that was 1,281 ESPN requests in twenty minutes, around 600/min, holding roughly a CPU core on a Pi and stalling the display loop it shares an interpreter with. The schedule pass now records what each request would need and the fetch runs afterwards for the display candidates only, picked the same way the caller picks what to show. show_odds_only widens that window threefold so the filter still has games to fall back on when the nearest ones have no lines posted yet. Candidate selection and display selection now share one implementation, so the games priced are the games shown -- picking candidates by a plain count while the display used a per-team quota could spend the whole budget on one favourite and leave another's game on screen without odds. Schedule collection also keeps enough games for the widest candidate window instead of stopping at the display limit, which had made the show_odds_only headroom inert.

Team logos now fit inside the panel instead of being scaled to 120% of the display height and cropped top and bottom. Text also renders with anti-aliasing off across all draw surfaces, so custom font sizes stay hard-edged; the default sizes were already on the font's pixel grid.

Fix missing team logos for NCAA men's basketball and NCAA baseball. The renderer discarded the logo directory the data fetcher had already resolved and used a hardcoded league map instead, which had no entries for ncaam_basketball or ncaa_baseball -- those leagues resolved to no directory and rendered every game with blank gaps where the logos belong, because the layout reserves the logo width whether or not a logo loads. The renderer now trusts the directory it is passed and falls back to the map, so a league added to the fetcher no longer needs a second table updated. A missing logo also warns once per team naming the paths searched, instead of logging at debug where nothing could see it.

Fix the NHL team picker, which listed UTA (retired code, labelled with the club's former name) instead of ESPN's UTAH, and omitted the Seattle Kraken entirely so they could not be selected at all. The list is now generated from ESPN and matches it exactly.

Fix config save failing with a 400 validation error. The per-league favorite-team pickers hardcoded several wrong team abbreviations that didn't match ESPN's (Rams LAâ†’LAR, White Sox CWSâ†’CHW, A's OAKâ†’ATH, Warriors GSWâ†’GS, Pelicans NOPâ†’NO, Knicks NYKâ†’NY, Spurs SASâ†’SA, Jazz UTAâ†’UTAH, Wizards WASâ†’WSH, NHL Kings LAKâ†’LA, Capitals WASâ†’WSH), so valid favorites were rejected on save and never matched games. Also removed the overly strict regex on the NCAA/MiLB free-text team fields so documented values like AP_TOP_25 are accepted.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed. Also enables the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL leagues by default so a fresh install shows odds immediately (college and MiLB remain opt-in).

Size the odds column to the actual 24px bases-diamond graphic for live baseball games instead of the unused away/home odds text width (up to 104px), removing up to ~80px of dead space before the inning info column.
